newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares retreat, led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares retreat, led by blue chips.

text.p: Nigerian shares slipped on Thursday, with blue chips suffering big losses, dealers said.
The all-share index fell to 8440.90 from 8445.44 on Wednesday. Dealers said the decline reflected a general perception in the market that the stocks were overpriced.
Thursday's laggards included Union Bank Nigeria Plc, which closed 28 kobo lower at 9.70 naira, and conglomerate Lever Brothers Nigeria Plc, which ended 20 kobo down at 27.30 naira.
Energy stocks also fell. African Petroleum Plc shed 25 kobo to finish at 55.00 naira, while Unipetrol fell 10 kobo to 67.30 naira.
But Guaranty Trust Bank, fresh from its first annual general meeting as a publicly quoted company on Tuesday, shot up 20 kobo to 5.75 naira after the release of its fiscal first-quarter results.
Earlier the bank said its after-tax profit rose to 120.1 million naira to the end of May from 116.1 million naira in the corresponding period of 1996.
NAL Merchant Bank Plc firmed five kobo to 8.45 naira, showing the banking sector as still promising, dealers said.
